title: Netflix's Melbourne NFL game matches YouTube's Brazil international viewership
dek: Netflix's 49ers-Rams game from Melbourne, Australia averaged 18.5 million U.S. viewers, matching YouTube's 2025 Chiefs-Chargers international game from Brazil in Week 1 domestic viewership. Netflix also drew 3.2 million international viewers compared to YouTube's 1.2 million internationally.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Netflix's first game in its expanded five-game 2026 package reached 18.5 million U.S. viewers, equaling YouTube's benchmark for international NFL broadcasts despite structural differences in measurement and distribution.
bottom_line: The 18.5 million figure represents parity in raw domestic numbers but masks methodological and distribution gaps that complicate direct valuation comparisons. Netflix's international reach (3.2 million across 200+ territories) substantially exceeds YouTube's (1.2 million), but whether that diversity translates to higher streaming rights value remains an open question for future NFL contract negotiations.
body: Netflix's 49ers-Rams game from Melbourne, Australia averaged 18.5 million viewers in the United States, matching the domestic viewership YouTube recorded for its 2025 Chiefs-Chargers international game from Brazil in Week 1, according to Front Office Sports. Netflix's Australia broadcast also drew 3.2 million viewers internationally, compared to YouTube's 1.2 million international viewers from the Brazil game.

The Netflix game, played on Thursday, represents the first of Netflix's newly expanded five-game league package this season. Netflix's Christmas Day doubleheader from the prior year averaged 23.7 million U.S. viewers, setting a higher precedent for the platform's NFL audience.

The parallel between the two broadcasts masks significant structural differences. Netflix used Nielsen audience measurement for the Australia game; YouTube used its own custom and revised viewership methodology, per Front Office Sports. Netflix is subscription-based, while YouTube's distribution is free. Netflix's game aired on Thursday; YouTube's Brazil game was on Friday.

Netflix's 49ers-Rams viewers tuned in from more than 200 countries and territories, according to Front Office Sports. The game faced heavy Thursday night sports competition, including US Open tennis semifinals, MLB pennant-race baseball, and a college football game involving No. 5 Miami.

The broader 2026 NFL season opening showed mixed viewership dynamics. The Wednesday kickoff game between the Patriots and Seahawks on NBC saw an 11 percent viewership drop, per Front Office Sports reporting. The game itself was decisive; San Francisco won in dominant fashion, which may have affected sustained viewer engagement as competitive stakes diminished.

Netflix's next game will be the league's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game, involving the Rams and Packers. Netflix will then broadcast another Christmas doubleheader and a Week 18 game with playoff implications.
